text:
maya: Quick thread — took a pass on the slope-band chart in console. Main problem: legend is too verbose and competes with the slopeband labels.
jonah: I noticed that too. On small widths the legend wraps to 2 lines and pushes the chart down.
lia: Can we collapse the legend by default for small multiples? Maybe show a tiny toggle icon that expands on hover/click.
pat: +1 for collapse. Also the slope bands currently use full opacity which hides lines behind them — consider 40% fill so gridlines and zero-line are still visible.
samir: Agree on opacity. Also accessibility: the slope-band fills need clearer aria descriptions. Right now screen readers read "band" for each series which is meaningless.
a11y-bot: Suggested aria: "slope band for <series name>, range <min> to <max>, baseline <zero or median>". Keep under 120 chars.
maya: Nice. For microcopy on the legend trigger I wrote: "Show series details" / "Hide series details" — thoughts?
lia: I like short: "Details" / "Hide" maybe with a visually-hidden label for screen readers: "Details for series <name>".
jonah: Implementation nit: the collapse should preserve keyboard focus order. If you tab into a collapsed legend, pressing Enter should expand and put focus into the first legend row.
pat: On smoothing: current toggle is global per dashboard. Can we add a per-chart smoothing override (e.g., "smoothing: auto | on | off")? Auto would follow user preference but allow explicit overrides.
samir: That helps for metrics where smoothing masks spikes. We should also surface an inline hint: "Smoothing hides short spikes; toggle off to inspect anomalies." small, muted copy under the toggle.
maya: UX ask: if outlier dimming is enabled, how do we surface that to the user? Right now it looks like a bug when a dot is faded.
lia: Suggestion: when dimming is active, add a subtle badge near the legend: "Outlier dimming on". Clicking it opens a tooltip explaining thresholds and a link to "configure outlier policy".
jonah: For the threshold UI, recommend a slider with sample preview and a small sparkline thumbnail that updates as you move it. Helps non-technical PMs understand impact.
pat: CSS accessibility note: ensure contrast ratio of the legend toggle icon against the background meets 4.5:1 when focused. Right now focus ring is a pale blue at AA fail.
a11y-bot: Accessibility checklist entry: "legend toggle focus contrast >= 4.5:1; keyboard expand/collapse; aria-expanded on toggle; descriptive aria-labels for slope bands".
samir: Copy tweak for the slope-band tooltip: current "range" -> propose "expected range" or "typical range (90th - 10th percentile)" — clearer about what band represents.
maya: Good call. Also consider adding a tiny info icon next to the band label that opens a short explanation, rather than overloading the tooltip.
lia: On small-multiples layout: when legend collapsed, align chart tops so rows line up vertically. Right now some charts shift because their legend heights differ.
jonah: Implementation approach: fixed legend container height for collapsed state, use overflow hidden + gradient fade on long lists with "show more" link.
pat: Two quick dev constraints: GPU-rendered canvas expects opacity changes to happen in the shader — we should avoid per-point DOM manipulations. We can supply a uniform alpha for band fills and a per-series dropout via a mask texture. I'll file an infra note.
maya: OK action items: 1) Lia to draft microcopy and hidden-label phrasing. 2) Samir to write aria copy and add checklist. 3) Pat to prototype alpha/shader approach and share perf notes. 4) Jonah to spec legend collapse interaction and keyboard behavior. I'll follow up with a tiny Figma screen update. :thumbsup:
lia: Will do — I'll post copy variants in #design after mockups.
samir: I'll add a short a11y test plan and pair with QA on the keyboard flow.
pat: I'll drop a short note in eng-runtime about shader approach and a sample perf run.
jonah: I'll create a tiny PR for the collapse toggle and demo it in staging.
maya: Thanks all — aiming to ship the legend/contrast/smoothing tweaks in the next sprint.
jonah: :rocket:
